column1: 1|是 for identity|是 links a subject to a noun identifying it. Do not use 是 before an ordinary descriptive adjective in this pattern.
2|吗 at the end of a question|Keep statement word order and add 吗 at the end to form a yes–no question.
3|不 for habitual negation|Place 不 before the verb. Negating the existence expressed by 有 usually requires 没有.
4|The measure word 本|Use 本 for books, 杯 for cups of drinks, and 辆 for vehicles. The number precedes the measure word.
5|在 for location|在 introduces the place where a person or thing is located.
6|的 for possession|Possessor + 的 + possession. This example is not the emphatic 是…的 construction.
7|了 for completed actions|Here, 了 after the verb marks a completed action. Not every reference to the past requires 了.
8|过 for past experience|过 marks experience. 去过 means having been somewhere; 正在去 means being on the way there.
9|正在 for an ongoing action|Place 正在 before the verb to describe an action in progress.
10|Comparisons with 比|Use A 比 B + adjective. 不比 does not automatically mean that A has less of the quality than B.
11|给 to introduce a recipient|给 + person + verb introduces the recipient or beneficiary of an action.
12|得 for degree and manner complements|得 follows the verb and introduces a description of manner or degree. Distinguish it from 的 and 地.
13|把 with a specific object|Use 把 + specific object + verb + result or location. 不 and 没 usually precede 把.
14|Passive sentences with 被|Use affected subject + 被 + agent + action. Keep the participants' roles clear.
15|除了…以外 with additional information|In addition to Chinese, the speaker also knows English. 还 adds information; 只 restricts the scope.
16|一边…一边… for simultaneous actions|Use this pattern for two actions happening at the same time. The subject must normally be able to perform both.
17|先…再… for a sequence|先 introduces the first action; 再 introduces the next intended action. Do not use 又 to instruct someone to repeat an action here.
18|只要…就… for a sufficient condition|只要 introduces a sufficient condition. Distinguish it from 只有…才…, which states a necessary condition.
19|即使…也… for a hypothetical concession|即使 introduces a hypothetical concession; 也 shows that the result remains unchanged.
20|不仅…而且… to add emphasis|The two clauses add information or increase emphasis, usually in the same evaluative direction.
21|虽然…但是… for contrast|The second clause contrasts with the expectation created by the first. Here, 还是 emphasizes that the result occurred anyway.
22|无论…都… for an unchanged result|无论 combines with a question word or alternatives. 都 shows that the result does not depend on the choice.
23|与其…不如… to prefer an alternative|Compare two approaches and recommend the second. Keep the two clauses parallel.
24|The result complement 好|准备好 means that preparation has reached its intended result. Result complements are not simply past-tense markers.
25|尽管…仍然… for concession|In this concessive pattern, 尽管 introduces circumstances despite which the result still occurs. Distinguish it from 尽管 meaning to go ahead and do something.
26|除非…否则… for an exception|除非 introduces an exception to the rule in the next clause. Read the scope of negation carefully.
27|既然…就… for an accepted premise|既然 presents a condition as accepted; 就 introduces a conclusion or advice.
28|以免 for an outcome to avoid|以免 introduces an unwanted outcome. 以便 usually introduces a desired purpose.
29|未必 to limit certainty|未必 means not necessarily. It does not assert with certainty that something is not better.
30|凡是…都… for everyone meeting a condition|凡是 introduces all members who meet a condition; 都 completes the statement about the whole group.
31|并非…而是… to correct an explanation|Reject the first explanation and replace it with the second. This pattern does not merely add information.
32|之所以…是因为… for cause and result|The result follows 之所以; the cause follows 是因为. Do not reverse the cause-and-result relationship.
33|一旦…就… for a triggering condition|一旦 emphasizes that a consequence or action follows when a condition arises.
34|与其说…不如说… to refine a description|Compare which description is more accurate. The second clause adjusts or clarifies the first.
35|不见得 to express uncertainty|Do not infer quality from participant numbers alone. 不见得 limits how certain the judgment is.
36|相较于 to introduce a comparison point|The opening phrase sets the comparison point. Compare the same aspect in the rest of the sentence.
37|诚然…然而… to acknowledge a limitation|Acknowledge a point while limiting the conclusions that can be drawn from it.
38|鉴于 to introduce grounds for a decision|鉴于 introduces the basis for a decision. Distinguish existing evidence from the intended purpose.
39|在于 to identify the key issue|关键在于 identifies the central issue. 能否 retains both possibilities: whether something can or cannot happen.
40|有待 for work still to be done|有待 indicates unfinished work. It does not mean that a conclusion has already been established.
41|基于 for the basis of an analysis|基于 marks the basis of an analysis. Hypotheses still require separate verification.
42|无从 for a lack of means or basis|Here, 无从 means that the missing data leaves no basis for judging the cause, not merely that there is no reason.
43|固然…但… to limit an inference|Acknowledge the importance of expanding scale, but reject the inference that it can replace improvements in quality.
44|倘若 for a hypothetical condition|倘若 introduces a hypothetical condition. The next clause describes a conditional consequence, not an unconditional fact.
45|乃至 to extend the scope|乃至 introduces a wider scope or a higher degree in a progression.
46|尚且…何况… for an even stronger case|Use the already strong case in the first clause to emphasize that the second case applies even more strongly.
47|与否 to retain both possibilities|合理与否 means whether something is reasonable or not. Do not omit the negative possibility when paraphrasing.
48|归根结底 for an underlying conclusion|This phrase introduces a judgment about an underlying cause or essential point after considering several factors.
49|并不意味着 to block an inference|A statistical association does not establish causation. Notice exactly what is being denied.
50|充其量 for an upper limit|充其量 sets an upper limit on what the available evidence can support.
51|未尝不是 for a cautious affirmation|The double negative allows a cautiously positive judgment. It is not an absolute assertion.
52|毋庸置疑 for a limited point of certainty|This phrase marks the point that is not in doubt. Do not extend that certainty to the interpretation that remains disputed.
53|换言之 to restate an implication|Restate the implication of the previous statement without adding a conclusion that goes beyond the evidence.
54|无可厚非…但… for qualified acceptance|Accept the aim of efficiency while requiring fairness to limit its pursuit. A concession is not unconditional approval.
